newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Anderson to sell Argentine assets.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Anderson to sell Argentine assets.

text.p: Canada's Anderson Exploration Ltd plans to sell Argentine oil assets it acquired through its 1995 takeover of Home Oil Co Ltd, chairman and chief executive J.C. Anderson said on Wednesday.
"We're going to put it out to competitive bid and we'll see what comes in the door," Anderson told reporters after his company's annual meeting.
He declined, however, to say what the firm expected to take in from a sale of the assets.

The assets to be placed on the block include interests in the Bajo Baguales and Atuel Norte exploration concessions, located in the Neuquen Basin, and a 100 percent stake in the Refugio Tupungato producing block in the Cuyo Basin. Both are located in west-central Argentina.
Anderson said Refugio Tupungata was producing about 1,600 barrels of oil per day.
"The fiscal regime is good but the operating regime is a lot different than it is (in Canada) and the exploration is very pure exploration -- it's grassroots stuff," he said.
"It takes a lot of capital and a lot of time and I believe we could better apply that capital in Canada."

Earlier on Wednesday Anderson reported much-improved results in the first quarter ending December 31. The company posted net earnings of C$37.2 million or C$0.31 per share, up from C$8.8 million or C$0.07 per share in the same period last year.
It said cash flow rose sharply to C$118.5 million or C$0.98 per share from C$69.4 million or C$0.58 per share.
Anderson said the company expected to drill about 600 oil and gas wells in Canada in 1997, about twice as many as last year.
Capital expenditure for the year was budgeted at about C$400 million, up from C$256 million in 1996, he said.

He said he expected the company's natural gas production to rise to 550 million cubic feet per day in 1997 from 506 million last year. Oil and gas liquids output was expected to average 35,000 barrels per day, a jump from last year's 29,500, Anderson said.
He said Anderson's 1997 budget was based on assumptions of West Texas Intermediate crude oil averaging US$22.50 and natural gas averaging C$1.90 per thousand cubic feet.
Anderson said the C$1.18 billion Home Oil takeover had translated into big benefits for both firms' shareholders, and he was not ruling out the possibility of making another corporate acquisition.

"We won't shy away from trying another one if we see upside," Anderson said. "We look at most of the buses that come down the street and if one stops in front of the building, we'll run out, kick the tyres and take a look at it."
